results.name: wl_subcompositor-wp_viewporter
results.shows: Subsurface order and viewport: red placed above green (place_above), blue placed below the window (place_below, seen only through its transparent right third), and a 64×64 four-colour buffer cropped to its white quadrant and scaled to 100×100 (wp_viewport set_source + set_destination).

results.name: xdg_wm_base-foot
results.shows: foot (wayland-native terminal) mapped and focused: it answered xdg_wm_base.ping with pong, acked each configure once (invalid_serial is now enforced), and asked for the theme's frame through xdg-decoration.

results.name: xdg_wm_base-gtk4-zenity
results.shows: A GTK 4 / libadwaita dialog with its own decorations: GTK 4 answers ping, acks configures once and creates its xdg_surface before any buffer (invalid_surface_state and unconfigured_buffer are now enforced).

results.name: xdg_wm_base-qt-featherpad
results.shows: A Qt 6 editor (FeatherPad) on Wayland: xdg-shell with the new error checks, xdg-decoration (server-side frame from the theme).

results.name: linux-dmabuf-vkcube
results.shows: vkcube through the Vulkan WSI: its buffers pass the new zwp_linux_buffer_params_v1 out_of_bounds checks (offset + stride × height inside each dmabuf).

results.name: wp_fifo_manager_v1-wp_commit_timing_manager_v1-wp_linux_drm_syncobj_manager_v1-vkcube
results.shows: vkcube's FIFO present mode through Mesa's Vulkan WSI on the new protocols: every frame waits on the fifo-v1 barrier the one before set, carries a commit-timing-v1 target time, and explicit-sync acquire and release points (linux-drm-syncobj-v1) on timelines it imported; no protocol error.

results.name: xdg_system_bell_v1-wp_color_manager_v1-foot
results.shows: foot rang the terminal bell (BEL) through xdg-system-bell-v1 (its default bell.system=yes), on its own surface (LordOS plays its alert sound unless Do Not Disturb is on), and described its surfaces as sRGB through color-management-v1 (a parametric image description set on each). No protocol error.

results.name: egl-es2gears
results.shows: An EGL client: its buffers (dmabuf or shm through Mesa's Wayland EGL) and xdg-shell flow pass the new checks.

results.name: chromium
results.shows: Chromium (Ozone/Wayland): subsurfaces, viewporter, xdg-shell, xdg-decoration, xdg-activation and the data device with the new error checks; no protocol error.
